Will use `ACTION_SCROLL_BACKWARD` and `ACTION_SCROLL_FORWARD` instead of `ACTION_SCROLL_LEFT` and `ACTION_SCROLL_RIGHT` since it also has a vertical layout.
`ACTION_SCROLL_BACKWARD` and `ACTION_SCROLL_FORWARD` were removed in latest version of accesskit, and only kept for compatibility, they are aliases for `UP` and `DOWN`.
So for vertical it should be `if` with LEFT/RIGHT and UP/DOWN branches.
I think it should not have all 4 actions registered at the same time, since it will show up as if it has both scroll directions, while there's only one.
We can register the `EditorScrollBox` as an abstract class and we only add two actions if it's vertical or horizontal.
Yes, it looks fine.

Do these classes need to be exposed?

This is mainly for documentation on how to use the new class and make it usable in Editor Plugins. I’ll make a change to address https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/109496, and I think it’s worth documenting. If not, we can replace the docs with inline code comments in the class instead.

Exposing it with EditorPlugins in mind requires a proposal, to clarify use-cases. See https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/3850 for example. Sounds useful, but had pretty much 0 interest, so it was closed. Not being exposed then allowed to [freely change the "API"](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/71685) of ViewPanner.

As for the documentation, the new class looks rather self-explanatory. It's basically a ScrollContainer with extra buttons. We don't usually put doc comments in the code, unless it's a core class with some important considerations.

Also makes `_validate_property()` not called.
This doesn't make much sense. You can just call `_update_buttons()`, it's a single line either way.
Too much code. You don't need to check status of each signal separately.

It can be useful if we want to move the Mouse Select modes to the left/right sides of the 2D and 3D editors. https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a0c1dfc1-5495-4a67-a141-22d7851840c6 Example from Aseprite.

> This looks like unused code. The property is not defined. Also makes `_validate_property()` not called.

It extends `BoxContainer` that's why i have this method to update the layout when `BoxContainer::vertical` is changed.
Seems like `BoxContainer` is not meant to be extended, it's better to extend `Container` class instead since there is no signal for orientation changing and `set_vertical` is not a virtual method.
But it shouldn't be added until we actually decide to do that. In most cases such code just ends up unused forever.
Makes sense to me, since it's not exposed anymore we can only support horizontal layout for this PR to avoid having unused code.

On RTL layout it says scroll to the `begin` instead of `end`, and to fix this it will result in 4 translated lines instead of just 2, so we can consider replacing both translations to say `Hold Ctrl to scroll to the far left` and `Hold Ctrl to scroll to the far right`.

I think putting the menu buttons into a Scroll Box is a weird UX, I haven't seen menu buttons be scrollable like this. 
It is also inconsistent, since to save space it can already be collapsed to a main menu button with an Editor Setting, there doesn't need to be 2 different ways to allow it to be smaller.

Ideally we would just switch to the collapsed main menu when there isn't enough space.
However I think it would need custom code to detect when it is too small (or something like https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/12397), so this can be changed later in a future PR.
Main screen plugins _might_ eventually get converted to docks, so the top buttons would become a TabBar.
